paper-end-end-multi-agent-2026.summary: This work presents a multi-agent AI system for personal finance that combines synthetic data generation, budget optimization, and investment advisory through a five-stage pipeline blending Bayesian demographic modeling, rule-based transaction simulation, GAN-based refinement, and LLM-driven enrichment. The system aims to produce realistic financial transaction data while protecting user privacy and supporting downstream advisory decisions. In Stage 3, the authors train CTGAN 'using the open-source implementation from the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) library' to refine synthetic transactions and model complex statistical dependencies, running it as one generative stage among several in the pipeline.

paper-online-digital-tools-expert-2026.summary: This paper describes digital tools developed within the EU BIORADAR project to help users benchmark, upload and analyze Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) data across the fertilizer, textile and packaging sectors. It combines Environmental Footprint benchmarking, synthetic data generation via an in-house statistical decomposition algorithm, and clustering/decision-tree analytics in a web-based self-assessment tool. The Synthetic Data Vault (Patki et al. 2016) is cited only in the reference list, with no SDV code, concept, or synthesizer actually used or described in the text.

paper-postoperative-delirium-lung-resect.summary: Predicts postoperative delirium after lung cancer resection where the real cohort is too small to train on, and adds LIME so the prediction can be inspected. The training set is 2,000 synthetic records generated with SDV from Figshare data; the test set is 570 real patients. SDV is run as the sole generator, and the small-sample framing the paper is built around only works because it stands in for the missing training cohort.

paper-redm-regression-guided-diffusion-2.summary: This paper proposes REDM, a regression-guided diffusion model for generating virtual samples to augment sparse labeled soft-sensor training data across semiconductor process stages (CVD, Etching, CMP), coupling a diffusion process with a regression objective and a quality-aware filtering mechanism using Sliced Wasserstein Distance and cosine similarity. It benchmarks REDM against TVAE, CTGAN, SMOTE, and TabDDPM as generative baselines with publicly available source code, showing REDM yields higher downstream regression R^2. CTGAN and TVAE, both cited to the CTGAN paper, are run as comparison baselines against which REDM's virtual samples are evaluated.
paper-redm-regression-guided-diffusion-2.needs: Both TVAE and CTGAN are cited to reference [8] (the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper), a mis-citation for TVAE which originates elsewhere; not clear whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package or an independent reimplementation was run, though 'publicly available source code' suggests the former.

paper-smogan-synthetic-minority-oversamp.summary: This paper proposes SMOGAN, a two-stage oversampling framework for imbalanced regression that first generates synthetic samples in sparse target regions with an existing oversampler and then refines them with DistGAN, a distribution-aware GAN trained with an adversarial loss augmented by a Maximum Mean Discrepancy objective, tested across 23 imbalanced regression datasets. The authors' own reimplemented DistGAN, not any SDV library code, carries the empirical programme. The metadata indicates a citation to the CTGAN paper, but no passage naming CTGAN, SDV, or any related component was found anywhere in the extracted full text.

paper-syngeneva-generator-agnostic-evalu.summary: This paper proposes SynGenEva, a generator-agnostic evaluation protocol for synthetic tabular data that standardizes preprocessing and introduces multi-perspective evaluation (global fidelity, conditional fidelity, downstream utility) across heterogeneous datasets and generators. The protocol is demonstrated on three datasets (Heart Disease, Wine Quality, NASA Turbofan) using three representative generators from different modelling families. Among these, the Gaussian Copula-based generative model, credited to Patki et al., is run as one of three benchmarked synthesizers alongside CTGAN and TVAE to compare synthetic data quality across fidelity and utility metrics.
paper-syngeneva-generator-agnostic-evalu.needs: Not explicit whether the SDV package itself (vs a reimplementation) was used to run Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, and TVAE; no import/package name or hyperparameter list is quoted in the visible excerpts.

paper-synthetic-tabular-generation-stora.summary: This conference paper compares four generative models—CTGAN, TabDDPM, TabSyn, and TabDiff—for synthesizing hard-disk-drive performance metrics (IOPS, latency) in data storage systems, addressing scarcity of proprietary performance data. The authors evaluate the synthetic outputs using visual inspection plus quantitative metrics including TVComplement, KSComplement, detection scores, and machine learning efficacy scores. CTGAN is run as one of the evaluated generators via the SDV library, which is used as the baseline synthesizer, and SDV's shape/trend similarity and detection-based quality metrics are used to score all four methods' synthetic output.
paper-synthetic-tabular-generation-stora.needs: Full text not obtained; affiliations and precise mechanism of CTGAN invocation (via SDV package vs. custom implementation) could not be confirmed.

paper-driven-predicting-remaining-useful.summary: This paper reviews data-driven remaining-useful-life prediction methods for electronic components and presents a case study on silicon carbide MOSFETs, combining feature selection, synthetic data augmentation, and probabilistic neural network architectures. The best RUL model in the case study was trained on a dataset augmented with synthetic samples, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines using only 4 of 22 features. CTGAN, described by the authors as 'implemented in the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) Python library,' is run as the synthetic data generator that produces the augmented training data underlying the paper's headline result.
paper-driven-predicting-remaining-useful.needs: Full text not obtained; author affiliations and any hyperparameter details (e.g., CTGAN constructor settings) could not be verified, and the degree to which conditional sampling specifically was leveraged is unclear.

paper-framework-create-evaluate-select-2.summary: This paper proposes a framework for generating, evaluating, and selecting among synthetic datasets to support survival prediction modeling in oncology research. The metadata indicates it cites both the CTGAN (NeurIPS 2019) and the original SDV (DSAA 2016) papers, suggesting synthetic tabular data generation methods from the SDV family are part of its pipeline, but no citing sentences, abstract, or full text were available to confirm how they are used. SDV's CTGAN and/or SDV framework appear to be cited as sources for the synthetic data generation approach, with the exact role (generator, baseline, or background citation) unclear from the evidence.

paper-framework-concrete-durability-asse.summary: This paper develops a machine-learning framework to predict chloride and sulfate ingress into concrete, using a GAN to augment a small laboratory dataset (403 chloride and 172 sulfate points) and a Bayesian Neural Network to make uncertainty-aware predictions, achieving R2 values of 0.95. The framework is aimed at durability assessment, service life estimation, and structural health monitoring. CTGAN is cited as the generative adversarial network approach used for tabular data augmentation.
paper-framework-concrete-durability-asse.needs: Full text needed to confirm whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev package (api_user) or reimplemented (port); abstract alone does not name CTGAN explicitly.

paper-adaptive-differentiable-trees-stre.summary: Introduces soft Hoeffding trees, a differentiable and inherently interpretable tree model for online learning that grows in the Hoeffding style while routing instances softly, so it can be trained by gradient descent and adapt to concept drift without losing the readability of a decision path. The evaluation needs long drifting streams that no public dataset supplies, so CTGAN is trained on real tables from the PMLB repository and sampled to emulate their distributions across streams of one million instances, into which ten abrupt drifts are injected by oversampling a randomly chosen class; a further scalability experiment generates ten million drift-free instances the same way. CTGAN is thus run as the data-generation engine for the paper's stream experiments while the paper's own contribution is the tree model, the pattern where an SDV generator powers one part of a study about something else.

paper-decoding-non-linearity-complexity-.summary: This paper explores deep tabular learning architectures (DNF-Nets, TabNet, encoder-decoder models, CNNs) as alternatives to tree-based ensembles for modeling highly skewed, wide-range materials science data such as creep resistance and high-temperature properties. It benchmarks these against XGBoost and LightGBM, finding XGBoost fastest but deep models competitive on non-linear, skewed distributions. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) is mentioned only in passing in the introduction as a generative approach for synthesizing tabular data, with no experiment run using it.

paper-enhancing-intrusion-detection-netw.summary: This conference paper compares GAN-based and diffusion-based synthetic data generation for augmenting malicious network traffic data used to train 5G intrusion detection ML models, further applying explainable AI to interpret model predictions. The authors implement CTGAN (via its DataTransformer/DataSampler/discriminator components) as the GAN-based tabular data generator and compare its output against TabDDPM diffusion-generated data for IDS training. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN, is run as one of the two main generative approaches whose synthetic data underpins the paper's empirical evaluation.

paper-gaussdb-aisql-composable-cloud-202.summary: This paper presents GaussDB-AISQL, a composable cloud-native SQL system that integrates AI model training and inference directly into a data warehouse, aiming to reduce data movement and simplify AI workflows via SQL-like syntax. Experiments show performance gains up to 19x over baseline approaches across various dataset scales. To test system performance at scale, the authors used the SDV synthesizer to fit an internal IP dataset and generate synthetic training data ranging from 3 GB to 1024 GB.

paper-generative-augmented-nearest-neigh.summary: This conference paper proposes a hybrid framework that augments a small, imbalanced student-performance dataset (156 students) using CTGAN-generated synthetic records, then trains an interpretable k-Nearest Neighbor classifier on the combined data. Using stratified 5-fold cross-validation, the authors show accuracy improving from 85% to 92% and minority-class recall from 70% to 85% relative to a real-data-only baseline. CTGAN is run as the core synthetic-data generator, conditioned on the outcome label to oversample the minority 'Fail' class, making it the engine behind the paper's entire empirical result.

paper-isomapgen-framework-early-predicti.summary: This paper proposes IsoMapGen, a framework combining tripartite feature extraction with a gated attention model to enable early prediction of peak ground acceleration (PGA), a key parameter in seismic hazard assessment. The work appears to target earthquake early-warning or seismic risk applications, though the full methodology is not available in this evidence. CTGAN is cited in the reference list, but the metadata gives no indication of how it is used within the framework, such as for data augmentation or as a baseline comparator.

paper-machine-learning-predict-gold-2025.summary: This paper develops a machine-learning workflow to predict the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSP) positions of gold nanostars from their seedless synthesis conditions, combining data collection, feature selection, synthetic data generation, and regression modeling (RF, SVR, XGB). To address the small dataset (144 samples), the authors compared four data augmentation methods—bootstrapping, SMOTE, GMM, and CTGAN—ultimately selecting bootstrapping as the best-performing approach. CTGAN was run as one of several candidate synthetic data generators and benchmarked against the other methods before being set aside in favor of bootstrapping.

paper-modeling-viscosity-infiltration-ki.summary: This paper develops machine-learning models to predict the viscosity of silicate melts that infiltrate thermal barrier coatings on aviation turbines, combining 7188 experimental data points with 60,000 synthetic samples to train accurate predictors (R2 > 0.97), then uses these models plus infiltration experiments to link melt composition to coating degradation kinetics. CTGAN is run to generate the large synthetic dataset that supplements the small experimental dataset used to train the viscosity predictors.

paper-optimizing-time-use-pricing-2025.summary: This paper proposes a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning approach for time-of-use pricing at public EV charging stations, using dedicated agents per time slot to jointly optimize station profit and grid load stability. The training data is a synthetic EV charging dataset derived from the Caltech ACN dataset, expanded to cover a much longer time span. CTGAN is used as the generator to augment the real Caltech dataset into the synthetic training data underlying the entire empirical study.

paper-optimizing-understanding-amorphous.summary: This materials-science study uses correlation analysis and causal discovery (DirectLiNGAM) alongside a genetic-algorithm-optimized Gaussian process model to identify optimal amorphous silicon nitride deposition parameters for GaN high-electron-mobility transistors, aiming to make black-box ML optimization more interpretable. The abstract and available evidence give no indication of synthetic data generation or evaluation being part of the study. The work cites the TGAN (2018) paper, but this appears only as a bibliographic reference with no discernible engagement in the visible text.

paper-covid-tvae-logistic-regression-202.summary: Flattens chest X-rays for COVID-19, pneumonia and normal cases into a tabular matrix, cuts the dimensionality with PCA, upsamples the reduced features with TVAE, and classifies with logistic regression at 85% accuracy, with SHAP reporting how many components carry each label. TVAE is one step in that pipeline and ships in SDV, but no library is named, so the mechanism is unconfirmed.

paper-ga-ctgan-ionizing-dose-2025.summary: Predicts radiation damage to bipolar junction transistors from total ionizing dose, where each data point requires exposing a device in a radiation facility. GA-CTGAN pairs a genetic algorithm with CTGAN to optimise the generator, a named derivative from a nuclear technology institute.

paper-preserving-logical-functional-depe.summary: This paper introduces the notion of logical dependencies among attributes in tabular data, alongside the established concept of functional dependencies, and proposes a Bayesian measure to quantify such logical dependencies. It compares several state-of-the-art synthetic tabular data generation algorithms across public datasets to test whether they preserve these dependency types, finding that functional dependencies are generally not preserved while some models can retain logical dependencies. CTGAN is included among the synthetic data generators evaluated in this comparative study.

paper-rac-gan-iterative-dual-2025.summary: This paper proposes RAC-GAN, an end-to-end trainable framework that combines a GAN-based generator for oversampling with a reinforcement-learning ranker for undersampling, jointly optimizing both operations to improve classifier performance on imbalanced tabular datasets. It is evaluated on 11 real-world imbalanced datasets against heuristic and state-of-the-art baselines. CTGAN is run as one of several baseline oversampling methods in the comparative experiments.

paper-synthetic-tabular-methods-attacks-.summary: A survey covering the state of the art in synthetic tabular data generation, spanning probabilistic graphical models and deep-learning approaches (GANs, VAEs, diffusion, LLM-based methods), and surveying attacks (e.g. membership inference) and defenses against them. The paper describes CTGAN's mode-specific normalization for mixed discrete/continuous columns and explains how TVAE reuses CTGAN's feature-modeling framework within an encoder-decoder architecture, but runs no experiments with either model itself. CTGAN and TVAE are discussed in prose as prior-art methods the survey explains, not executed as generators or baselines.

paper-trans-ctgan-transformer-enhanced-2.summary: This paper proposes Trans-CTGAN, a modified version of CTGAN that inserts multi-head Transformer attention into both the generator and discriminator to better model inter-feature correlations, while removing CTGAN's PacGAN component, and evaluates it on five public tabular datasets against CTABGAN, CTGAN, TVAE and TabDDPM using correlation-matrix distance and ML utility metrics. The paper fundamentally redesigns CTGAN's architecture, including its conditional vector design, mode-specific normalization, and training sampling scheme, into a new Transformer-augmented generator, and separately runs CTGAN and TVAE (via the Synthcity framework) as comparison baselines throughout the experiments.

paper-unpacking-predictive-relationships.summary: This work applies an explainable ensemble machine-learning framework to predict properties of graphene oxide-reinforced cementitious nanocomposites, addressing the scarcity of experimental data through some form of data augmentation, per the title. The reference list cites both the CTGAN (NeurIPS 2019) paper and the original SDV (DSAA 2016) paper, suggesting CTGAN/SDV may have been used to generate the augmented training data, but no citing sentence or abstract text confirms this. SDV/CTGAN appear only as cited works in the metadata record, with no direct textual evidence of how they were used.

paper-method-privacy-safe-synthetic-2024.summary: This paper proposes DP-ACTGAN, a Differentially Private Auxiliary-Classifier Conditional Tabular GAN for generating privacy-safe synthetic health records, adding a classifier to preserve data utility and a differential-privacy noise mechanism to resist membership-inference attacks. It is evaluated on three hospital datasets against plain CTGAN and DPGAN for machine-learning utility, statistical similarity, and privacy leakage. The model is built directly on CTGAN's conditional tabular GAN architecture and loss function, described as 'an improvement on past studies like [12, 18]' with a loss 'consistent with the one described in [12]' (the CTGAN paper), while CTGAN itself is also run unmodified as a comparison baseline in the experiments.

paper-fully-automated-platform-synthetic.summary: This paper introduces STNG, a fully automated synthetic tabular neural generator that runs eight parallel synthetic-data generators (four generic single-function methods and four STNG-modified variants) alongside an Auto-ML validation module that scores and compares the resulting synthetic datasets across twelve healthcare and other tabular datasets. The generic single-function methods used as both baselines and building blocks for STNG's modified versions are Gaussian copula, CopulaGAN, CTGAN, and TVAE -- the core single-table synthesizers of SDV's ecosystem, which the paper explicitly credits as 'the largest open source ecosystem for synthetic data generation and evaluation.' SDV's Gaussian copula, CopulaGAN, CTGAN and TVAE synthesizers are run directly as the generic comparators against which STNG's own modified generators are benchmarked, forming the backbone of the entire empirical evaluation.

paper-imbalance-fault-diagnosis-method-2.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid deep learning fault-diagnosis framework for imbalanced gearbox vibration datasets, using a k-nearest-neighbor maximum trend diffusion algorithm optimized via grid search to synthesize minority-class fault samples, then fusing temporal and spatial features for classification. It reports improved diagnostic accuracy and F1 score over other models across different imbalance ratios on two gearbox datasets. CTGAN (Xu et al.) is cited only in passing among related imbalance-learning works, not run in the proposed method.

paper-gan-generating-fair-synthetic-2024.summary: This paper proposes Bt-GAN, a healthcare-domain GAN that generates fair synthetic EHR data by combining an information-constrained fairness-aware data generation process with score-based weighted sampling to preserve sub-group densities, evaluated on MIMIC-III. In its related-work survey of prior synthetic health-data generators it describes HealthGAN, noting that HealthGAN used the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) for categorical encoding. SDV is only cited in passing as part of another cited work's pipeline, not used or run by the authors themselves.

paper-clipartgan-application-pix2pix-gen.summary: This paper proposes ClipArtGAN, a Pix2Pix-based GAN model that converts photos of objects into corresponding clip art images, trained and compared against a CycleGAN baseline on three collected datasets. It reports that ClipArtGAN outperforms CycleGAN and Google Images-based search in generating representative clip art. CTGAN is cited only once in the introduction as an example of a conditional GAN modeling multimodal continuous data distributions, with no use in the actual work.

paper-epa-gan-electric-power-2024.summary: This paper proposes EPA-GAN, a GAN-based table synthesis model for anonymizing electric power marketing data, adding feature encoders, feedback mechanisms, and a Wasserstein-GP loss to generate privacy-protective synthetic tabular data while preserving machine-learning utility and statistical similarity to the original. The authors compare EPA-GAN's ML-utility and statistical-similarity scores against CWGAN, TableGAN, and CT-GAN baselines, and also cite CTGAN's mixed-variable feature-encoding approach as inspiration for their own encoder design. CTGAN (from the SDV family) is used as one of several comparison generators in the evaluation and is also cited for its variable-type feature encoding concept, without evidence that the sdv-dev package itself was invoked.

paper-frugal-generative-modeling-tabular.summary: This paper introduces Gmda, a frugal deep generative model for tabular data that aligns true and synthetic distributions by minimizing discrepancies in sample fractions within sampled hyper-rectangles, rather than relying on large adversarial or diffusion architectures. It reports extensive experiments on artificial and real-world datasets, comparing Gmda's fidelity, precision/recall, machine-learning efficacy, and model size/training cost against TVAE, CTGAN, and TabDDPM. TVAE and CTGAN are run as baseline generators throughout the empirical evaluation, with CTGAN's conditional generative mechanism also cited as a design inspiration for Gmda's own class-conditional variant.

paper-generating-synthetic-tabular-image.summary: This paper proposes I2TGANF, a framework that transforms tabular data into two-dimensional feature matrices so that off-the-shelf image GANs (DCGAN, WGAN) can be trained to generate synthetic tabular data, which is then reconstructed back into tabular form. Experiments on three imbalanced tabular datasets compare classifiers trained on real, sampled-balanced, and GAN-synthesized data. CTGAN is used with its default settings as the baseline tabular GAN against which I2TGANF's image-GAN-based synthetic data is compared for downstream ML classifier performance.

paper-generative-augmentation-differenti.summary: This paper addresses the non-IID data distribution problem in decentralized (federated) clinical machine learning by proposing a generative data augmentation approach combined with differential privacy guarantees. The work targets healthcare settings where patient data across institutions is heterogeneous and privacy-sensitive, aiming to improve model training via synthetic augmentation while bounding privacy leakage. It cites the CTGAN paper, but the evidence available does not show whether CTGAN itself, or a derivative built on it, was actually run.
paper-generative-augmentation-differenti.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run directly, modified with differential privacy, or merely cited as related work.

paper-landslide-susceptibility-ctgan-202.summary: Studies how to balance a landslide inventory for susceptibility mapping in Lianghe County, Yunnan, where mapped landslides (positive samples) are far scarcer and non-landslide cells (negative samples) far less reliable than a classifier needs. Two problems are attacked at once: negative samples are screened with a self-training semi-supervised SVM, and positive samples are augmented with CTGAN, a plain GAN and SMOTE in increments of 50 to 250 synthetic records. Three classifiers, a 1D CNN-LSTM, a random forest and a gradient boosted decision tree, are trained on ten environmental factors and scored by AUC and F1. Screening the negatives alone lifts AUC from 0.778, 0.869 and 0.849 to 0.837, 0.936 and 0.877, and the best model in the study is a random forest trained with 200 CTGAN-generated positive samples at AUC 0.962. A t-SNE comparison of real against synthetic points is used to argue that SMOTE output sits tightly around the real data while CTGAN output fills the distributional space, giving more diversity while still simulating the overall distribution. The paper is in the index because CTGAN is the generator behind its best result: it is credited to Xu et al. 2019, its conditional generator with training-by-sampling and its Gaussian-mixture normalization of continuous columns are reproduced in the method section as the reason it suits landslide data mixing continuous factors such as elevation and slope with discrete ones such as lithology and land use, and its synthetic samples are what the winning random forest is trained on. No library is named anywhere in the text, so the entry keys to the ctgan component on the strength of the method description and the runs reported.

paper-machine-learning-assisted-stroke-2.summary: This study examines systemic mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation abnormalities as predictors of postoperative stroke in continuous-flow left ventricular assist device patients, using LASSO and Random Forest models on blood leukocyte protein data to achieve an AUC of 0.93. The authors describe balancing their small clinical dataset with SMOTE oversampling rather than any SDV-family tool. The citation to the CTGAN paper appears in the sentence describing this SMOTE-based class balancing, with no evidence CTGAN itself was run.
paper-machine-learning-assisted-stroke-2.needs: Full text not available; the citation appears attached to a SMOTE description rather than any CTGAN usage, so it is unclear whether CTGAN was used elsewhere in the paper or this is purely a mis-citation.

paper-smoe-ctgan-2024.summary: Treats disclosure risk and utility as two conflicting objectives rather than one, evolving a population of generators under NSGA-II with a reinforcement-learning agent choosing which of three loss functions trains each offspring, and adds an Improvement Score to select a final generator before risk climbs. The resulting model, SMOE-CTGAN, keeps CTGAN's backbone, conditional vector, training-by-sampling, Gumbel-softmax and PacGAN discriminator settings unaltered and replaces only the optimisation around them, so it is a named variant built directly on CTGAN.

paper-generative-methods-single-cell-202.summary: This paper investigates whether data augmentation of scRNA-seq reference data can improve bulk RNA sequence deconvolution, proposing a new generative method, sc-CMGAN, that selects cell marker genes stepwise before training a GAN. The authors benchmark sc-CMGAN against three existing generative methods across four public datasets and three deconvolution algorithms, finding sc-CMGAN more robust overall. Gaussian Copula, CTGAN and TVAE from the SDV family are run as the benchmarking generative baselines against which the authors' new synthesizer is compared.
paper-generative-methods-single-cell-202.needs: The citation (refs 22,23) attributes Copula, CTGAN, and TVAE jointly to what appears to be the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper; this may be a mis-citation since Gaussian Copula and TVAE are not from that paper, but the paper's own wording is preserved.

paper-prediction-time-temperature-transf.summary: The paper compares multiple machine-learning algorithms (including a multilayer perceptron and an Ft-Transformer) for predicting time-temperature-transformation diagrams of NiAl alloy from a database assembled from multiple metallurgical data sources. To enlarge this database the authors apply data augmentation designed to keep synthetic samples physically realistic, and cite the original Synthetic Data Vault paper in connection with this augmentation step.
paper-prediction-time-temperature-transf.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether SDV software was actually run for data augmentation or merely cited as a conceptual reference.

paper-skypewebc-conditional-generative-a.summary: This paper proposes SkypeWebC, a network covert channel that hides secret data in Skype's WebRTC traffic via packet-length padding, using a conditional GAN to generate covert traffic that is statistically indistinguishable from legitimate traffic; experiments show state-of-the-art encrypted-traffic classifiers cannot detect the covert channel above 54% accuracy. The authors build their own CTGAN-style generator/discriminator from scratch, describing its architecture, loss function, and training algorithm in detail rather than invoking the sdv-dev package. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional-vector design are reimplemented and extended (adding label/position information) to drive the entire generation pipeline that the paper's results rest on.
paper-skypewebc-conditional-generative-a.needs: The paper cites CTGAN [19] but presents its own from-scratch generator/discriminator architecture and training algorithm rather than the sdv-dev CTGAN package, so this is judged a reimplementation (port) rather than direct library use; not fully verifiable whether any SDV code was actually invoked.

paper-beet-productivity-copulas-2024.summary: Analyses sugar beet productivity from field trial data, where each observation is a growing season and the record is correspondingly short. The title names Gaussian copulas and GANs as the generation methods, placing SDV's copula machinery in an agronomic setting; no abstract is indexed, so the role is read from the title alone.
paper-beet-productivity-copulas-2024.needs: fetch the full text and confirm which copula implementation is used

paper-comparative-analysis-effectiveness.summary: This conference paper presents a comparative study of several GAN variants -- DCGAN, SRGAN, and CGAN -- evaluated on image benchmark datasets (CIFAR-10, MNIST) using metrics such as FID and standard GAN loss functions, aiming to guide architecture selection for generative modeling tasks. The paper's empirical work is entirely image-focused and does not include CTGAN among the evaluated models. CTGAN is cited only as one of the SDV-family works referenced in the paper's discussion of GAN variants, with no evidence it was run or engaged with in the tabular-data sense.
paper-comparative-analysis-effectiveness.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm the exact sentence or context in which CTGAN is cited, though the abstract's image-only scope suggests it is a passing mention only.

paper-gene-environment-pathways-cognitiv.summary: This eLife study uses large-scale longitudinal data from the Adolescent Brain and Cognitive Development Study (6,602 children) and a novel structural equation modeling method to test how genetic polygenic scores and familial/neighborhood environmental factors jointly shape cognitive intelligence and childhood psychotic-like experiences, adjusting for confounders. The authors note elsewhere that a synthetic dataset was generated with conditional GAN to imitate the structure of their final study sample, but a full-text search found no further engagement with the method beyond this citation. CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019) is cited only in passing as the source of the conditional GAN technique used to produce that synthetic dataset, with no described running or evaluation of the library itself in the retrievable text.
paper-gene-environment-pathways-cognitiv.needs: The quoted sentence describes an actual synthetic-data generation step, yet the full-text scan reports no SDV mention outside the bibliography; unresolved whether this reflects a supplementary/author-response analysis not captured in the retrieved sections or a citation-only reference.

paper-investigation-security-models-iot-.summary: This conference paper studies targeted adversarial attacks on tabular-data ML models used for IoT/mmWave line-of-sight detection with DeepMIMO-generated data, proposing use of the LowProFool algorithm and GAN-based synthetic adversarial sample generation. In its related-work review of tabular data synthesis methods, it describes the TGAN approach as a GAN model for generating relational tables with continuous and discrete variables via multimodal distribution modeling, but does not run it in its own experiments.
paper-investigation-security-models-iot-.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether TGAN or related SDV code was actually run beyond this single citing sentence.

paper-mlgan-addressing-imbalance-multila.summary: This paper proposes MLGAN, a GAN-based oversampling method for multilabel datasets that generates synthetic minority-label samples to address class imbalance, comparing its resampling strategy against MLSMOTE across six datasets and five multilabel learners. The authors build their generator by adopting CTGAN's architecture -- its conditional generator, mode-specific normalization, and training-by-sampling of the conditional vector -- reimplemented within their own multilabel framework rather than run via the SDV package. CTGAN's conditional tabular GAN design is the architectural foundation the authors' own generator is built on.
paper-mlgan-addressing-imbalance-multila.needs: No import, package name, or constructor parameters appear; the description of CTGAN's architecture strongly suggests an authors' own reimplementation adapted for multilabel data rather than running the sdv-dev package, hence classified as port.

paper-sapipin-observations-pin-code-2023.summary: This paper introduces SapiPin, a new dataset of PIN-code typing dynamics collected from 112 subjects on touchscreen devices, and studies how inter-key latency distinguishes slow, medium, and fast typists. Using half the dataset to train synthetic data generators, the authors evaluate how effectively an attacker could impersonate genuine typing rhythms using generated samples, finding slow typists hardest to attack. The SDV package is run directly to produce the synthetic typing data via its Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, and TVAE synthesizers, which are compared against each other and against real data for attack effectiveness.

paper-flood-forecasting-tabgan-2023.summary: Forecasts floods from meteorological records, motivated by how poorly mitigation has kept pace with the damage. CTGAN is applied to numerical augmentation of the existing record rather than to free generation, a distinction the paper draws explicitly.

paper-bearing-degradation-tgan-2022.summary: Predicts bearing degradation from vibration signals under the constraint that run-to-failure experiments are expensive, so the training set is small. Vibration is decomposed by discrete wavelet transform with the base wavelet chosen by mutual information, a generative model is fitted to the resulting wavelet coefficients and sampled for artificial coefficients, statistical features are computed from real and artificial coefficients alike, and ensemble bagged trees and Gaussian process regression are trained on the combined feature vector, reaching an average RMSE of 0.0045. The generator is TGAN, credited in the text to Lei Xu and Kalyan Veeramachaneni and cited as arXiv 1811.11264, so the SDV-family model actually run here is CTGAN's predecessor rather than CTGAN, and it is the production generator of the pipeline.

paper-guided-auto-discovery-low-2022.summary: This work develops an AI-guided framework to discover low-carbon, cost-effective mix designs for ultra-high performance concrete (UHPC), likely using machine-learning surrogate models trained on limited experimental data. The metadata shows it cites the original SDV DSAA 2016 paper, but no citing sentence, abstract, or full text was available to determine how SDV concepts were actually used. SDV is referenced as a cited prior work, with its role (e.g., possible synthetic data augmentation for materials data) unverifiable from the available evidence.
paper-guided-auto-discovery-low-2022.needs: No abstract, citing sentence, or full text available; cannot determine whether SDV was run, adapted, or merely cited in a UHPC materials-discovery context.

paper-regeneration-poisoned-datasets-202.summary: This paper proposes methods for detecting and regenerating corrupted or missing data in soft-copy datasets, combining a modified Adamic Adar link-prediction technique with K-means clustering, regression, and deep learning models, and reporting 78% accuracy versus 50% for K-means. It also discusses extending GANs, noted for image generation success, to the problem of lost data regeneration. TGAN (cited as 'Synthesizing tabular data using generative adversarial networks') is mentioned only as prior work using Conditional GANs, with no experiment run.
paper-regeneration-poisoned-datasets-202.needs: Full text not obtained; abstract and citing sentences give no indication SDV/TGAN code was actually executed, only discussed as related work on GAN-based generation.

paper-counterfactual-examples-augmentati.summary: This paper explores whether counterfactual examples can be used to augment small training datasets, comparing this approach against GAN-based tabular data augmentation on the Adult-Income dataset. Experiments show counterfactual-based augmentation performs favorably against generative approaches. The paper cites and runs Tabular GAN (TGAN) as a baseline generator to produce comparison synthetic data for augmentation.

paper-generating-evaluating-cross-sectio.summary: This paper proposes a framework for generating and evaluating synthetic cross-sectional electronic healthcare data that preserves data utility while protecting patient privacy, demonstrated on the Indian liver patient dataset and a UK primary care dataset. It surveys prior generative approaches to synthetic data, including Patki et al.'s SDV work on relational databases, as related-work context rather than as a tool used in the framework. SDV's HMA-based relational synthetic data generation approach is only cited descriptively, not run in the reported experiments.
paper-generating-evaluating-cross-sectio.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentence available, so it is unclear whether SDV is engaged with further in the body beyond related-work description.

paper-stan-synthetic-network-traffic-202.summary: This paper introduces STAN, a CNN-based autoregressive neural architecture that models both temporal dependencies and cross-attribute dependencies to generate realistic synthetic network traffic data for cybersecurity applications where real data sharing raises privacy concerns. STAN is evaluated on simulated and real netflow datasets against several baselines using likelihood, distribution comparisons, domain-knowledge tests, and downstream anomaly-detection accuracy. CTGAN is run as one of four baseline generators (alongside GMM, BN, and WPGAN) and is shown to perform poorly compared to STAN across most tests, serving purely as a comparison point rather than as part of STAN's own architecture.

paper-automl-survey-state-art-2020.summary: A comprehensive survey covering the AutoML pipeline -- data preparation, feature engineering, hyperparameter optimization, and neural architecture search -- summarizing representative methods and open problems in the field. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni) is mentioned only as a bibliographic reference within a broader list of GAN-based data synthesis works, with no discussion or use in the body text. TGAN, the SDV-family tabular GAN precursor to CTGAN, is only cited, not run or engaged with.

paper-one-hot-encoding-privacy-2020.summary: This paper proposes HealthGAN, a WGAN-based approach to embed high-cardinality categorical electronic health record features into lower-dimensional dense vectors and then generate synthetic embedded EHR data to preserve patient privacy while retaining utility for machine learning. The method builds a novel variant of a categorical encoding approach the authors attribute to the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) paper, adapting the idea in their own pipeline rather than running SDV's software. SDV is cited only as the origin of the categorical encoding concept they modify, with no SDV library or code executed.
paper-one-hot-encoding-privacy-2020.needs: Unclear exactly which SDV encoding mechanism (RDT transformer) inspired the 'novel variant'; no SDV code appears to be run.

preprint-counterfactual-residual-augment.summary: This paper proposes Counterfactual Residual Data Augmentation (CRDA), a model-agnostic technique for tabular regression that generates new training samples by perturbing features while preserving a base predictor's residual noise, improving MSE for MLP and XGBoost regressors on small-sample datasets. It benchmarks CRDA against deep generative baselines including TabDDPM, TVAE, and CTGAN, reporting hyperparameters such as CTGAN's batch size, embedding dimension, generator/discriminator dims, learning rate, and pac. CTGAN and TVAE are run as comparison baselines that the authors' method is shown to outperform.

paper-tabquerybench-2026.summary: Scores synthetic tables by whether analytical queries return the same answers on them as on the real data, rather than by distance between distributions, and shows the two can diverge: a generator can look strong on distance metrics while collapsing the support a filtered or grouped query depends on, with high-cardinality columns and local conditional queries the sharpest failures. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the eleven generators put through the benchmark, each packaged and tuned over epochs, batch size and embedding and hidden dimensions.
paper-tabquerybench-2026.needs: integration for a benchmark paper is a convention gap: nothing is proposed here, so the eleven generators are evaluation subjects rather than baselines against a contribution, which makes baseline_only a poor fit; recorded api_user at importance 3 because CTGAN and TVAE are run but are two rows of eleven

paper-sdv-vs-synthcity-comparison-2025.summary: Head-to-head evaluation of six tabular generators drawn from two libraries — SDV's Gaussian Copula, CTGAN and TVAE against Synthcity's Bayesian Network, CTGAN and TVAE — on UCI energy-consumption data, scored on statistical similarity and on downstream predictive utility at balanced and 1:10 sampling ratios. Synthcity's Bayesian Network takes fidelity; SDV's TVAE takes predictive utility at 1:10; neither library wins outright and the recommendation turns on documentation and ease of use, where SDV is judged the better tool for practitioners. SDV is run throughout, three synthesizers plus its statistical comparison functions, and it is half the subject matter rather than a baseline.
paper-sdv-vs-synthcity-comparison-2025.needs: shard 04 already carries a repository whose evidence is a second-hand analysis of this same arXiv paper (2506.17847); check the two entries do not double-count.

preprint-propensity-score-matching-gan-2.summary: This preprint proposes hybrid propensity-score matching approaches that use GAN-generated synthetic patients to reduce sample loss in observational causal-inference studies, testing partial and full hybrid matching in simulations and in a real-world EHR dataset of mechanically ventilated COVID-19 patients evaluating prone positioning. The authors trained CTGAN on simulated and imputed patient records to generate large pools of synthetic 'counterfactual' patients for matching. CTGAN is run via the open-source Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) library, using its default hyperparameters, as the sole generator underpinning the entire empirical programme.

preprint-raregraph-synth-knowledge-guide.summary: This preprint proposes RareGraph-Synth, a knowledge-graph-guided continuous-time diffusion model that generates privacy-preserving synthetic EHR trajectories for ultra-rare diseases by using meta-path scores from a unified 8-million-edge biomedical knowledge graph to modulate the diffusion noise schedule. The model is evaluated for fidelity (via categorical MMD) and privacy (via DOMIAS membership-inference attacks) against unguided diffusion and GAN baselines. Its baseline GAN comparator is stated to follow 'the RCGAN implementation in Xu et al.', citing the CTGAN paper, indicating the authors built their own GAN baseline based on that design rather than running the SDV library itself.
preprint-raregraph-synth-knowledge-guide.needs: Unclear whether the 'RCGAN implementation' the authors built is a genuine reimplementation of CTGAN's design or a mis-citation naming confusion with a different recurrent GAN model; no SDV library code or CTGAN-specific terminology (mode-specific normalization, conditional vector) appears in the body text.

preprint-synthetic-tabular-generation-ho.summary: This preprint investigates how federating a synthetic tabular data generator across multiple simulated clinical sites affects the fidelity-privacy trade-off of synthetic Acute Myeloid Leukemia data, comparing centralized, evenly distributed, imbalanced, and non-IID federated scenarios across varying node counts. The generative model chosen was Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN), explicitly implemented via the Synthetic Data Vault package, with its default architecture (256-unit hidden layers, 2x10-4 learning rate, 128-dim embedding, batch size 500) adapted for a federated learning wrapper. SDV's CTGAN is thus run as the sole generator underpinning the entire empirical evaluation of fidelity and privacy across all federated scenarios.

preprint-latable-large-tabular-models-20.summary: This paper proposes LaTable, a tabular diffusion model designed to be trained jointly across many heterogeneous datasets using textual metadata, aiming toward a generative Large Tabular Model that supports few- and zero-shot synthetic data generation. The authors evaluate LaTable against several established tabular generators across 78 datasets, measuring downstream ML utility and synthetic data quality metrics. CTGAN and TVAE, from the CTGAN paper, are run unmodified as two of several baseline generators compared against LaTable's in-distribution and out-of-distribution generation performance.

preprint-partial-multivariate-model-fore.summary: This preprint proposes PMformer, a Transformer-based 'partial-multivariate' time-series forecasting model that captures dependencies only within sampled subsets of features rather than across all features (complete-multivariate) or none (univariate), showing it outperforms both extremes on several benchmarks. The work is unrelated to synthetic tabular data generation; it cites the CTGAN paper only in passing to justify using Sigmoid/Tanh output-layer activations for a theoretical assumption. CTGAN is mentioned solely as a citation supporting an activation-function design choice, never run or engaged with as a synthesizer.

paper-taegan-2024.summary: Introduces TAEGAN, a tabular GAN whose generator is a masked auto-encoder given a self-supervised warmup and a weight-matrix-based sampling scheme, and reports that on small datasets it improves machine learning efficacy over larger language-model-based generators. It inherits CTGAN's feature engineering, one-hot categorical encoding and variational Gaussian mixture decomposition of continuous columns following mode-specific normalization, and generalizes CTGAN's conditional vector into a representation that lifts the restriction to categorical components and to a single component per condition; CTGAN and TVAE are separately two of the seven baselines, run from synthcity, and the reality and fidelity metrics follow the SDMetrics documentation.

preprint-tabmda-tabular-manifold-augment.summary: This paper proposes TabMDA, a training-free manifold data augmentation method that uses a pre-trained in-context tabular model (e.g., TabPFN) to embed and augment training data via repeated in-context encoding with varied data subsets, improving performance for any downstream classifier across tabular datasets. CTGAN is cited only in passing as an example of the computationally expensive generative modeling approaches to tabular data augmentation that the paper's method avoids, with no experiment using it.

preprint-distributed-meteorological-pred.summary: This preprint studies data augmentation methods -- SMOTE and GAN-based oversampling -- to address class imbalance in tabular weather data (rainy vs. non-rainy day classification) under both centralized and federated learning settings, using an Australian weather dataset. The empirical work centers on the authors' own GAN and SMOTE-based augmentation pipelines rather than any SDV tool. CTGAN is listed among the works cited by the paper's metadata, but no CTGAN or other SDV-family mention could be located in the extracted full text, suggesting only a passing bibliographic citation.
preprint-distributed-meteorological-pred.needs: Full text search found zero SDV-family mentions despite the citation record; the actual citing sentence (likely in a reference list not captured) could not be verified, so importance/integration are best-guess.

preprint-review-ensemble-learning-augmen.summary: This paper is a large computational review comparing nine data augmentation methods (including SMOTE, ADASYN, ROS, and CT-GAN) against ten ensemble learning methods for classification with class imbalance, evaluated across many benchmark datasets. It concludes that traditional oversampling methods such as SMOTE and ROS generally outperform CT-GAN-based augmentation while being far cheaper computationally. CT-GAN is described and implemented by the authors as a small custom network (three hidden layers, MSE loss, Adam optimizer) rather than the SDV-dev CTGAN package, drawing on CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional generation ideas as one of several data augmentation baselines tested throughout the study.
preprint-review-ensemble-learning-augmen.needs: The described CT-GAN architecture (3 hidden layers, MSE loss) diverges sharply from the actual CTGAN design, confirming a from-scratch reimplementation rather than use of the sdv-dev library.

preprint-self-attention-differentially-p.summary: This preprint proposes DP-SACTGAN, a self-attention-based conditional GAN for differentially private tabular data synthesis that draws on CTAB-GAN+'s data modeling scheme and adds layer normalization and an auxiliary classifier to improve utility under differential privacy. It is evaluated against CTAB-GAN+, DP-GAN, and PATE-GAN plus CTGAN on the Adult and King housing datasets using accuracy/AUC/F1, statistical distance metrics, and membership-inference attacks. CTGAN, credited with introducing mode-specific normalization for GANs, is run as one of several comparative baseline models in the experiments.
preprint-self-attention-differentially-p.needs: Evidence does not indicate whether the CTGAN baseline was run via the sdv-dev/CTGAN package or an independent reimplementation, so the api_user vs. port distinction cannot be confirmed.

preprint-learning-continually-sequence-g.summary: This paper develops a dynamical-systems/adaptive-dynamic-programming formulation of continual learning on sequences of graphs, casting the balance between forgetting and generalization as a two-player Stackelberg game and proving convergence to a solution, with experiments on graph benchmarks. As part of its hyperparameter search procedure, the authors fit a Gaussian copula to the top-performing hyperparameter configurations and sample 1,000 new candidate hyperparameters from it. SDV's Gaussian copula concept is cited as the source of this technique and applied as a minor auxiliary step in the training pipeline, not as the paper's main contribution.
preprint-learning-continually-sequence-g.needs: Unclear whether the authors used the SDV/copulas package or their own implementation to fit the Gaussian copula for hyperparameter sampling.

paper-survivalgan-time-to-event-2023.summary: Identifies two failure modes specific to generating survival data, short-sightedness in the time axis and poor coverage of the censoring process, and proposes SurvivalGAN, which generates covariates first and then draws the time-to-event from a separate survival model conditioned on them, so that Kaplan-Meier curves of the synthetic data track the real ones. The tabular encoder it depends on is CTGAN's: a Gaussian mixture is fitted per continuous feature and the encoder built from it, following Xu et al. directly, and CTGAN and TVAE are also two of the five generators the result is measured against across four clinical datasets.

paper-synthpop-plus-population-2023.summary: Builds Synthpop++, a country-scale synthetic population for India that layers four data sources of differing granularity, using iterative proportional updating where marginals exist and a learned generator where they do not, and validating the result against held-out survey distributions. CTGAN supplies the attributes marginals cannot reach: it is trained on Individual and Household microdata and conditioned on age and sex to attach weight, height, comorbidities and job description to each synthetic person, and the paper selects it over statistical alternatives for handling mixed types, high dimensionality and imbalanced categoricals.

preprint-private-synthetic-hierarchical-.summary: This paper studies differentially private synthetic data generation for hierarchical datasets (e.g., people within households), formalizing the problem of hierarchical query release and introducing algorithms (HPD-Fixed, HPD-Gen) evaluated on American Community Survey and Allegheny Family Screening Tool data. CTGAN is mentioned only in a bibliography list of works on synthetic tabular data generation for purposes other than query release, without being run or engaged with technically. CTGAN is cited only as related work outside the paper's own private query-release focus.

preprint-turning-tables-biased-imbalance.summary: This paper introduces the Bank Account Fraud (BAF) suite, the first publicly available, privacy-preserving, large-scale suite of realistic tabular datasets derived from an anonymized real-world bank account opening fraud detection dataset, designed to stress-test both performance and fairness of ML methods under temporal shift, class imbalance, and controlled biases. The suite's six dataset variants were produced by training 70 CTGAN models via random hyperparameter search on privacy-perturbed applicant data, with omitted hyperparameters left at CTGAN's implementation defaults. CTGAN is run as the core generative engine that produces the entire synthetic dataset suite underlying the paper's contribution.

preprint-black-box-model-risk-2-2021.summary: A sub-chapter examining risks introduced by machine learning models in financial applications, focusing on the use of ML for pricing and hedging financial options, and cataloguing sources of model risk along with mitigation strategies. It is not a synthetic-data paper; TGAN (Xu and Veeramachaneni, 2018) is mentioned only in passing as an example of a technique offering missing-data imputation and outlier treatment.
preprint-black-box-model-risk-2-2021.needs: Full text not obtained; only a single passing citation sentence is available, so deeper engagement with TGAN cannot be ruled out or confirmed.

paper-conditional-counterfactual-explana.summary: Proposes a framework that trains a conditional generative model to emit counterfactual explanations in a single forward pass rather than by per-instance optimization, conditioning the generator on the desired target prediction and applying it across image, time-series and mixed-type tabular modalities. The tabular branch, named CF-CTGAN, is built directly on CTGAN: the generator and discriminator architectures are reused as-is from Xu et al., continuous features carry CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and categorical features its Gumbel-Softmax sampling, with CTGAN's conditional vector removed and replaced by conditioning on the target class.
paper-conditional-counterfactual-explana.needs: importance 5 follows the named-variant convention (CF-CTGAN reuses CTGAN's generator and discriminator as-is). Reviewable: the tabular branch is one of three modality branches (CelebA uses a ResNet encoder-decoder, ECG adapts RCGAN), so a reviewer applying the constrained-DGM precedent for a substrate that carries only part of the paper may prefer 4.

paper-boundary-calibration-gan-2021.summary: Adds a boundary-calibration loss to adversarial training that penalises generated points falling across decision boundaries approximated by classifiers pretrained on the real data, and reports that the resulting BWGAN and BMMDGAN raise the accuracy of models trained on synthetic data across four UCI tables and two image sets without losing sample quality. CTGAN supplies the machine-learning-efficacy criterion the paper adopts as its measure of model compatibility and is the tabular prior work it positions against, but it is not run.
